findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.comment: Observed food items to be stored on floor. Discussed with PIC, education was provided and items were moved to at least 6 inches off of ground. Ensure any food item is kept at least 6 inches off of ground.
findings.citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Observed a used, closed single service bowl to be resting in an in use rice cooker. Discussed with PIC, bowl was removed and rice cooker was emptied and remade. Ensure only rice is placed in rice cookers to prevent any possible contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Observed a container of noodles to be at 50F in cooler. Discussed with PIC, noodles were placed in a way that prevented the cooler air from dispensing evenly. Noodles were moved to bottom of prep cooler and later ran a temperature of 40F. Ensure any TCS item being cold held is kept at or below 41F.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
Observed 2 dishes to be resting in hand sink upon inspection. Discussed with PIC, dishes were moved to triple sink. Ensure hand sink is only being used to wash hands. 

5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED. 

(REPEAT) Observed food handling employee to wash and rinse hands in the prep sink, then re-engage in food prep behaviors. Employee should be washing hands in the hand sink. Hand sinks are for hand washing only. Preparation sinks are for food preparation only. Ensure employees know to wash hands only in the hand sink. Discussed with PIC and employee. COS. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 6/7/22.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.  

Observed all food handler’s licenses to be expired. Discussed with PIC. Ensure all other employees (not the certified food protection manager) re-take the online course. Print copies of the certificates for the facility. Ensure certification is completed by next routine inspection and copies are at the restaurant.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.comment:
2-102.11: Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, PIC shall demonstrate knowledge by:  (A) Having no Priority Foundation items; (B) Being a CFM; OR (C) Responding correctly questions as they relate to the specific FOOD operation. The areas of knowledge include C1 through C16.  

Multiple Foodborne Illness Risk Violations observed during this inspection. Among them, a situation where the main cook was observed to touch raw chicken, rinse their hands, then touch raw shrimp. A translater will be utilized in the future to help facilitate effective understanding of safety for relevant Foodborne Illness Risk Violations noted on today’s inspection.

findings.comment:
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED. 

The main cook was observed to rinse their hands in the 3 part sink and then to proceed to handle foods. This is not proper hand washing procedures. Education took place during the inspection.

findings.comment:
5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. 

1) On arrival, the hand sink next to the three part sink has shrimp in front of it partially blocking access to the sink. findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria.

On arrival, the sani bucket used for the kitchen is not registering a color change on either the inspector’s or facility’s test strips. Facility uses bleach (CL). Bucket was remade during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Proper cooling time and temperature
findings.comment:
3-501.14: (A) TCS FOOD shall be cooled within in 2 hours from 135F to 70F. Within 6 hours, FOOD shall cool from 135F to 41F or less. (B) TCS FOOD shall be cooled within 4 hours or less if prepared from ingredients at ambient temperature. (C) TCS FOOD received above 45F in compliance with LAWS shall be cooled within 4 hours. (D) Raw EGGS shall be received and immediately placed in EQUIPMENT with air temperature of 45F or less. 

1) Raw chicken is in the process of being prepared for the par cooking procedure used at the facility. Because of the lunch rush the chicken was left in a large wok style bowl and worked on as time permitted. Probing the chicken at different locations showed internal temperatures between 65F and 68F. PIC indicated that the chicken was only out of the cooler approximately 30 minutes to an hour. The back door is open (screen door closed) and the average temperature is in the mid 70s in the kitchen. Education took place and the chicken finished its prep process and was par cooked promptly. 

2) Par cooked chicken (after frying) is observed in several boxes (on a table) next to the back door of the facility. PIC stated that the chicken was cooling prior to placement in the walk-in. Internal temperatures are observed at 75F-77F. PIC indicated that the chicken was only out of the fryer around an hour. Education took place. Once the chicken reaches 135F in the cooling process it should be moved to the walk in cooler for rapid cooling so that it can meat the time/ temperature requirements required by the code. The chicken was moved into the walk in cooler during the inspection to correct the violation.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment:
3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned. 

A long handled scoop is observed stored in sauce with only approximately an inch of wood outside of the sauce. The rest of the handle is inside the sauce and does not allow for the handle to be gripped without contaminating the sauce. PIC instructed to store handles with adequate space on the handles that will not contact both foods (sauces) and employee hands.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment:
3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned. 

The spatula used for portioning rice is observed stored in a cup of standing water. PIC is instructed to store in use food contact utensils in an approved manner.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment: 3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). Raw beef is observed stored over cooked chicken in the walk in cooler. PIC was consulted and the items reversed in the cooler to abide by the requirements of the code. A hand out in both English and Mandarin was given to the PIC during the inspection.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11  (Pf) The hand sink in the facility was block on arrival by a pot and scoop as well as two sauce jugs on the floor in front of it. Hand washing sinks must be accessible at all times. The items were removed during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11  (C) On arrival, the hot water in the hand sink in the kitchen was observed to not be functioning correctly. Maintenance was conducted while the inspector was at the facility and the hot water began functioning correctly.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11  (P)  Raw chicken is observed stored above raw vegetables in the walk in cooler. The items were moved during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.citation_text:
3-304.12  (C) Store in-use utensils: 1) in the food with the handle above the top of the food item; 2) on a clean and sanitized surface; 3) in running water; 4) in a container of hot water maintained at or above 135 F.

The rice spatula was observed stored in a bowl of luke warm water. The issue was discussed and the spatula removed to correct.
